summary: An operating system manages computer hardware/software resources and provides services like process management. A process is an executing program with a Process Control Block (PCB) storing details such as state, program counter, and memory allocation. Processes transition through states: New, Ready, Running, Waiting (Blocked), and Terminated, based on CPU scheduling and resource availability. CPU scheduling algorithms include First Come First Serve (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Round Robin (RR), and Priority Scheduling.
